item.title: x64dbg: Open-source Windows debugger for malware analysis
item.description:
x64dbg: Open-source Windows debugger for malware analysis

x64dbg is an open-source user-mode debugger for Windows, optimized specifically for reverse engineering and malware analysis. It is designed for the binary debugging of executables for which source code is not available.

🔍 Overview

The tool serves as a binary debugger for Windows, targeting security professionals and developers who need to analyze compiled software. Key characteristics include:

  • An open-source user-mode debugger.
  • Optimized for reverse engineering and malware analysis.
  • Aimed at executables without source code.
  • A comprehensive plugin system allows users to add their own features.

🚀 Availability

Users can obtain the software through several methods:

  • Download snapshots from GitHub or SourceForge.
  • Extract the downloaded files in a location where the user has write access.
  • Optionally run x96dbg.exe to register a shell extension and add desktop shortcuts.
  • Compile the project from source using a few easy steps.

⚙️ Key Details

The tool supports both 32-bit and 64-bit executables. Users can run specific executables based on architecture:

  • Run x32\x32dbg.exe to debug a 32-bit executable.
  • Run x64\x64dbg.exe to debug a 64-bit executable.
  • Run x96dbg.exe to choose the architecture if unsure.

🧩 How It Works

The project relies on several external technologies to handle core functionality:

Component Technology / Source
Debugger core TitanEngine Community Edition
Disassembly Zydis
Assembly XEDParse and asmjit
Import reconstruction Scylla
JSON Jansson
Database compression lz4
Bug icon VisualPharm
Interface icons Fugue
Website tr4ceflow

💡 Why It Matters

x64dbg is a community effort that actively accepts pull requests. Contributors are encouraged to review the CONTRIBUTING document and start with “good first issues.” The project acknowledges specific individuals and groups, including Sigma for developing the initial GUI, all donors, and those adding issues. While the project previously received donations through BountySource and is now transitioning to GitHub Sponsors, it remains a collaborative open-source initiative.

#x64dbg #MalwareAnalysis #ReverseEngineering #WindowsDebugger #OpenSource

Source: x64dbg/x64dbg

item.title: REA: AI‑Powered Reverse Engineering Across Binaries and Apps
item.description:
REA: AI‑Powered Reverse Engineering Across Binaries and Apps

Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries. REA provides a single MCP for reverse engineering across binaries, applications, and runtime behavior.

🔍 Overview

  • “Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.”
  • “One MCP for reverse engineering across binaries, applications, and runtime behavior.”
  • “Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code.”
  • “REA returns findings with their evidence.”

🧩 How it works

  1. Choose your agents – supported agents include Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, and other agents.
  2. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions.
  3. Setup adds REA’s MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing configuration.
  4. Restart your agent afterward.
  5. The agent calls REA through the MCP, which inspects the target and traces relevant code, returning findings with evidence.

⚙️ Key details

  • “Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and other agents.”
  • “Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval.”
  • “Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine.”
  • “For native analysis, configure a provider first.”
  • “See the CLI and Evidence guide for native commands, provider selection, snapshots and scripting.”
  • “REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes.”
  • “Keep your installation up to date.”
  • “Bun global updates require Bun 1.2.17 or later.”
  • “With an older Bun release, upgrade Bun manually before running rea update.”
  • “To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed by the update.”
  • “Review the setup changes and restart your agent.”
  • “For one‑off CLI commands, use npx rea-agents@latest followed by the command.”
  • “With Bun, use bunx rea-agents@latest in place of npx rea-agents@latest.”

Supported agents

Supported Agent Status
Claude Code Supported
Codex Supported
Cursor Supported
Gemini CLI Supported
Grok Build Supported
other agents Supported

🚀 Availability

  • “Visit the REA website for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies.”
  • “See installation and setup for provider configuration and manual MCP registration.”
  • “For native analysis, configure a provider first.”
  • “Replace the path with your target, such as D:/apps/example on Windows.”
  • “Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand.”
  • “The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence.”

💡 Why it matters

  • Enables developers and security researchers to understand how a feature works, down to the binary level, using familiar analysis tools and AI agents.
  • Streamlines the workflow from agent selection to evidence generation, reducing manual setup and configuration effort.

#ReverseEngineering #AIAgents #MCP #SoftwareAnalysis

item.title: Paint.NET ships reverse-engineered Direct2D for WINE
item.description:
Paint.NET ships reverse-engineered Direct2D for WINE

Paint.NET has overcome a long-standing compatibility hurdle by shipping an internal, clean-room rewrite of Direct2D for use on WINE.

🔍 Overview

  • Direct2D has historically been the largest blocker for running Paint.NET on WINE.
  • Past efforts to implement Direct2D compatibility were insufficient for Paint.NET’s needs.
  • The team could not simply disable Direct2D usage in the application.

🧩 How it works

  • Paint.NET now includes a reverse-engineered implementation of Direct2D triggered by the /wine command-line flag.
  • The code lives in PaintDotNet.Windows.Direct2D1.Managed.dll.
  • The rewrite was produced by a reverse-engineering assistant referred to as “Claude.”

⚙️ Key details

  • The codebase totals roughly 180,000 lines, compared to about 700,000 lines for the rest of Paint.NET.
  • Development spanned multiple years, with the author noting over two decades of work on Paint.NET itself.
  • The assistant operated with high productivity at times, described as “the fury of 10 freshly unshackled Einstein genius-level 10x coders.”

Code quality and maintenance

  • Most of the reverse-engineered code was written in a “vibe coded” style, meaning it has not undergone thorough review.
  • The author could not realistically review the full 180,000 lines of code.
  • Resource management issues were identified and corrected, including missing COM reference counting (AddRef equivalents).
  • Architectural and design flaws were occasionally corrected after being flagged by the author.

Technical achievements

  • The assistant performed extensive reverse engineering to derive formulas for Direct2D’s built-in effects library.

🚀 Availability

  • The feature is available now when running Paint.NET with the /wine flag on WINE.

💡 Why it matters

  • This workaround enables Paint.NET to run on WINE without relying on incomplete or unavailable Direct2D implementations.
  • It demonstrates a practical path for applications to bypass platform-specific graphics limitations through clean-room reverse engineering.

#Paint.NET #Direct2D #WINE #reverseengineering #compatibility

Source: A quote from Rick Brewster
